current_wording: PCOS can fit either: if the message centres on periods, fertility, or other reproductive conditions (such as PMDD or endometriosis), use Pregnancy and reproductive health; if it centres on hormones, blood sugar, or cholesterol, use this code; use the other as secondary when both are present.
proposed_wording: Add: When a message lists several conditions from both codes without centring on one, the primary topic is the code with MORE of the named conditions (PCOS counts as reproductive); if tied, use the code of the first condition named. The other code is the secondary topic.
why: All 3 pilot coders chose T10 primary / T6 secondary, but the step-07 draft had T6 primary / T10 secondary. All 3 wrote that the rule assumes one centre and did not decide a list of equal conditions.
status: Not needed: topics are now a descriptive list (analyst decision, 2026-11-05)

current_wording: Add one secondary topic only if the message clearly also asks about a second subject.

why: 2 of 3 coders gave tennis elbow (the reason for the injection) as secondary and 1 did not; all 3 were unsure. The draft had it as secondary.
status: Not needed: topics are now a descriptive list (analyst decision, 2026-11-05)

why: All 3 coders noted that this rule clashed with the one-secondary limit when two condition topics and a supplement request are all present.
